verdicts.factCheck: I queried https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc myself on 2026-11-26. eth_getCode of 0xacb7e78fa05d562e0a5d3089ec896d57d057d38e returned 24,009 bytes with sha256 prefix 3b2a403251a0d27f, the same as codeSha256 in state/networks.json. eth_getLogs over blocks 0 to latest with the Donate topic 0x29ef05ca... returned an empty array, and the same query with the Initialize topic returned 143 logs, so the full range query works on this endpoint and the empty Donate result is real. eth_getLogs over 0 to latest with the ERC-6909 Transfer, Approval and OperatorSet topics returned 187 logs: 47 mints (from zero), 140 burns where the caller in the data equals from, and no transfer, Approval or OperatorSet log (last at block 30,328,827). eth_getStorageAt slot 2 (protocolFeeController) is zero; slot 0 holds owner 0xa107580f.... The work file out/4326/branches.json lists 387 JUMPI sites, 116 both, 193 one side, 78 never, 0 mismatches and 20,000 storage checks, matching the finding. I did not rerun the 20,000 transaction replay or the six out-of-window traces. The producer is closed, so the core premise (that a fault could exist only on unexecuted sides) cannot be tested further.
verdicts.codeCheck: PoolManager.donate (src/PoolManager.sol:256-276) calls Pool.donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480); settleFor is src/PoolManager.sol:305-307; clear is src/PoolManager.sol:310-319; the third-party allowance branch of _burnFrom is src/ERC6909Claims.sol:15-19, which a self burn skips, matching the 140 self burns. The overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp is src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:42-52 and is reached only from getNextSqrtPriceFromInput (SqrtPriceMath.sol:147). The protocol fee branch is Pool.sol:385-398 and needs protocolFee > 0, which only the controller can set (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41) after the owner appoints one (ProtocolFees.sol:29-32). The 100 percent fee guard is Pool.sol:311-316. The cited lines say what the finding says.
verdicts.corrections: The mechanism first lists the MIN clamp (Pool.sol:351) and getTickAtSqrtPrice near MIN_SQRT_PRICE as never executed and later says six pre-window swaps did execute both clamps on MegaETH; the final reduced list is the correct one. The protocol fee branch is reachable only through governance, so it does not belong among the paths an ordinary account can reach.

In out/999/branches.json the JUMPI rows at pc 20618 (SwapMath.sol:88), 20638 (SwapMath.sol:91) and 20672 (SwapMath.sol:100) have taken 0 and fallthrough 0, while the same rows on 4326 and 143 have both sides executed, so the replay tool counts these sites when they run. clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether the 512-bit paths of the Position fee copy of mulDiv (Position.sol:94-96), the amount > uint160 copy (SqrtPriceMath.sol:97) and mulDivRoundingUp at SqrtPriceMath.sol:105 can decide a balance.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Position.sol:93-96 takes prod1 != 0 only when the fee growth difference times liquidity is at least 2^256, which makes the correct result at least 2^128, and Pool.sol:192 reverts in toInt128 (SafeCast.sol:56-58). SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 is reached only from getNextSqrtPriceFromInput (SqrtPriceMath.sol:148) in the exhausting step of an exact-input swap (SwapMath.sol:75-82), so amountSpecifiedRemaining becomes 0 and Pool.sol:455 or :459 casts an amount above 2^160 and reverts (SafeCast.sol:40-43). SqrtPriceMath.sol:105 is reached only from getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput (:176) with amountOut = amountRemaining (SwapMath.sol:96-98), with the same revert. The SwapMath.sol:65 copy needs |amountRemaining| near 2^236; correct results then exceed any amountIn, so only a too-small faulty result changes the path, and that path exhausts the amount and reverts at Pool.sol:455/459. The clearance holds for correct execution. Under a hypothetical producer fault, a wrong small result at Position.sol:94 would not revert, but reaching it needs real fee growth of 2^128 per position, which only an attacker-made token in its own pool can produce, so no other user is exposed.
